turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — Scales in vitro microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using well-stirred and parallel-tube models.

Input: Compound data CSV with columns: compound_id (e.g. imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, ponatinib), CLint_uL_per_min_mg (microsomal intrinsic clearance), molecular_weight
Key steps:

PKNCA + well-stirred/parallel-tube models → predicted CLh (mL/min/kg) per compound
Hepatic blood flow scaling → extraction ratio (ER = CLh / Qh, where Qh ≈ 20.7 mL/min/kg) per compound


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh + ER per TKI) + clearance_summary.json (model comparison, low/medium/high extraction classification)

Decision gate: Flag compounds with ER > 0.7 (high extraction) as high-hepatic-clearance liabilities requiring formulation or dose-frequency adjustment; target ER < 0.3 for once-daily oral TKI candidates.

IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — BCR-ABL1 TKI Panel — Scales measured microsomal CLint to predicted human CLh and extraction ratio for 4 TKIs using the well-stirred liver model.

Input: bcr_abl1_tki_ivive_input.csv (auto-generated above) — 4 compounds with compound_id, CLint_uL_per_min_mg, molecular_weight, fu_plasma, fu_mic; model parameters: Qh = 20.7 mL/min/kg, fu_mic = 1.0
Key steps:

ivive_hepatic_clearance workflow → well-stirred model: CLh = (Qh × fu_plasma × CLint_scaled) / (Qh + fu_plasma × CLint_scaled) per compound
Extraction ratio calculation → ER = CLh / Qh; compounds classified as low (ER < 0.3), intermediate (0.3–0.7), or high (ER > 0.7)


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh in mL/min/kg + ER per TKI) + clearance_summary.json (model comparison + extraction class per compound)

✅ Your input CSV has been prepared and is ready. Click Run to launch the ivive_hepatic_clearance workflow with the parameters above — no manual data entry needed.

⚠️ Note: fu_plasma values have been included in the input file for the well-stirred model correction. Dasatinib (CLint = 220) is expected to flag as high extraction (ER > 0.7); Nilotinib (CLint = 12) is expected to fall in the low extraction range — exact values will be confirmed by the workflow output.

notes: Expected ordering: Dasatinib(33%) > Bosutinib(9%) > Imatinib(5%) > Nilotinib(0.7%)

ABL1 Kinase Inhibitor Pharmacophore Build & Screen — Derives a consensus pharmacophore model from four known ABL1 inhibitors and screens a compound library against it in a single workflow.


Input: Reference SMILES — Imatinib, Dasatinib, Bosutinib, Asciminib (4 ABL1 actives); Library SMILES — Gleevec-analog-1, Ponatinib, Terfenadine, Acetaminophen; min_features = 3


Key steps:

Pharmacophore tool → builds consensus model by extracting shared pharmacophoric features (H-bond donors/acceptors, hydrophobic centers, aromatic rings, positive ionizable) across all 4 reference inhibitors
Pharmacophore Alignment tool → aligns each library compound to the consensus model, scores feature matches, and filters hits meeting min_features ≥ 3



Expected output: Ranked hit list (CSV/SDF) with per-compound feature-match scores and alignment poses; compounds failing the min_features = 3 threshold flagged as non-hits (expected: Terfenadine and Acetaminophen likely rejected; Gleevec-analog-1 and Ponatinib likely retained)


Decision gate: Retain only compounds matching ≥ 3 pharmacophoric features with an alignment score above the consensus threshold — hits should then be triaged by ADMET profiling (hERG IC₅₀ > 1 µM, DILI risk = low) before progressing to docking.

BCR-ABL1 Campaign Safety-Potency Ranking — Ingests dual-assay IC50 data for 15 compounds and produces a composite rank separating potent, cardiac-safe leads from hERG liabilities.

Input: 30-row assay CSV (15 compounds × 2 assay types: IC50_BCR_ABL1 [nM] + hERG_IC50 [µM], dated 2026-03-15)
Key steps:

Assay Ingestion & Parser → pivots long-format CSV into per-compound potency + safety columns, normalizes units (nM → µM alignment)
Composite Scorer → computes selectivity index (hERG IC₅₀ / BCR-ABL1 IC₅₀), applies log-scaled potency score + cardiac safety penalty, generates weighted composite rank
Report Generator → produces ranked compound table, flagging hERG IC₅₀ < 1 µM as ⚠️ cardiac risk and BCR-ABL1 IC₅₀ < 10 nM as ✅ potent hits


Expected output: ranked_compounds.csv (composite score + individual assay columns + risk flags) + interactive HTML report + ranking_summary.json (top hits, flagged compounds, campaign statistics)

Decision gate: hERG IC₅₀ > 1 µM (cardiac safety threshold) AND BCR-ABL1 IC₅₀ < 10 nM (potency threshold) — compounds meeting both criteria advance; CPD009 (hERG 0.08 µM) and CPD010 (hERG 0.05 µM) are auto-flagged as withdrawn-drug analogues and ranked last.
